page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-8 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine belonging to the g2 server family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon processor with 8 dedicated vCPUs, 4 physical cores, and 2 threads per core running at 2.2 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 38 MB L3 cache, supporting instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512, and AES. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

A central feature of the g2-standard-8 is its single NVIDIA L4 GPU from the Ada Lovelace family, which provides 24 GB of dedicated VRAM. In benchmark testing, this hardware configuration demonstrates exceptional performance in machine learning workloads, achieving top-tier results in LLM inference speed for both prompt processing and text generation using small (135M) and medium (7B) models. Conversely, general CPU performance is more modest; single-core stress-ng, single-threaded compression, and Geekbench scores fall into the lower performance tier. Multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations perform in the average range.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the g2-standard-8 represents a specialized resource density tradeoff, offering entry-level GPU acceleration without the overhead of larger multi-GPU instances. Because it lacks local storage, workloads requiring high-speed local disk I/O must rely on network-attached storage. This server type is highly suited for low-to-medium scale LLM inference, graphics rendering, and GPU-accelerated compute tasks, while being less optimal for CPU-bound compilation or heavy single-threaded processing.
description: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-8 is a graphics-optimized server featuring an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor with 8 dedicated vCPUs, 4 physical cores, and 32.0 GB of system memory. It integrates a single NVIDIA L4 GPU from the Ada Lovelace architecture with 24 GB of VRAM, while offering no local storage. Performance benchmarks reveal a stark contrast between CPU and GPU capabilities: while single-core and multi-core CPU benchmarks, compression tasks, and Geekbench scores rank in the lower to average tiers, the instance delivers top-tier performance in LLM inference for small and medium models. This resource profile makes the g2-standard-8 highly cost-efficient for specialized workloads such as machine learning inference, small-scale AI model serving, and GPU-accelerated graphics processing, rather than general-purpose or CPU-heavy computing.
